name: חיבור שברים אלגבריים – גורם (u+v) ומכנים שונים (באנגלית)

functions.name: igcd2
functions.body: if q=0 then abs(p) else igcd2(q,mod(p,q))

questiontext:
Express the following as a single fraction in its lowest terms:

\[ \frac{{CT:0}}{{CT:1}}+\frac{{CT:2}}{{CT:3}}. \]

[[input:ans]]
[[validation:ans]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Treat the common bracket as one variable, bring the fractions to the lowest common denominator, add the numerators and cancel any common factor.
Step 1 — Treat the bracket as one variable
You can treat compound terms, \({{CT:4}}\) as a single variable when simplifying the above expression. Alternatively you can substitute \(w = {{CT:4}}\) and thereby simplify with a single variable:

\[ \frac{{CT:0}}{{CT:1}}+\frac{{CT:2}}{{CT:3}} = \frac{{{CT:5}}w}{{CT:1}}+\frac{{{CT:6}}w}{{CT:3}} \]

Step 2 — The common denominator
The lowest common multiple of the denominators is \(\operatorname{lcm}({{CT:1}},{{CT:3}})={{CT:7}}\). Expand the first fraction by \({{CT:8}}\) and the second by \({{CT:9}}\), then add the numerators:

\[ \frac{{{CT:5}}w}{{CT:1}}+\frac{{{CT:6}}w}{{CT:3}} = \frac{{{CT:10}}w}{{CT:7}}+\frac{{{CT:11}}w}{{CT:7}} = \frac{{{CT:12}}w}{{CT:7}} \]

Step 3 — Lowest terms and back to the variables
[[if test="{{CT:15}}"]]The numerator and the denominator have the common factor \({{CT:13}}\); cancel it. [[/if]]Put back \(w={{CT:4}}\):

\[ \frac{{CT:0}}{{CT:1}}+\frac{{CT:2}}{{CT:3}} = {{CT:14}} \]

on_true.feedback: You cannot simply add the numerators and denominators when adding fractions. You need to find a common denominator and then add the fractions. One option is to use the general rule: \(\frac{a}{c}+\frac{b}{d} = \frac{ad+bc}{cd} \)
